#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

blocks.text:
Now I understand the fix required. The blocking issue: mirror update steps run before any checkout, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` depends on workspace content. The reviewer suggested two bootstrap options:

1. Inline minimal "ensure mirror + one fetch" prelude, then extract script from the mirror: `git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"`.
2. `curl` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com.

The tricky thing: on the first post-merge run, the mirror contains the pre-merge tree — `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` doesn't exist in the pre-merge mirror either (until a fetch updates the mirror... wait, actually the mirror is a mirror of the GitHub repo. On the first post-merge run, if the mirror gets fetched/updated first, then `main:` in the mirror WOULD contain the script after fetch. But wait — the mirror could have fetched already? The mirror updates when CI runs. The first post-merge run happens because a push to main occurs; but does any job fetch the mirror before this one? Not necessarily.

Let me think carefully about the bootstrap options:

Option A: inline prelude — ensure mirror exists (clone if not), do one fetch, then extract `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` from the mirror's `main` branch and run it. On the first post-merge run, the inline fetch updates the mirror to post-merge main, so `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` exists. Design for the YAML steps — shared pattern at all 3 call sites:

        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" \

bash "$SCRIPT" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"

Actually macOS's /usr/bin/curl is 8.x on recent macOS, but older runners could have 7.64. `--retry-all-errors` was added in curl 7.71.0 (June 2020). macOS 12+ ships curl 7.77+. Safe enough. With `-f` and `--retry`, HTTP 5xx and transient errors retry; connection failures retry too. `--retry-all-errors` also retries 4xx which we don't want anyway (404 = bad pin, retrying won't help). Actually with --retry (without --retry-all-errors), curl retries on transient errors: timeouts, FTP errors, HTTP 408/429/5xx, connection refused/reset... AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.

  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. # pr-1665: gh-1644 [daily-publish] cli leg failed

## Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

blocks.text:
Now I understand the fix required. The blocking issue: mirror update steps run before any checkout, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` depends on workspace content. The reviewer suggested two bootstrap options:

1. Inline minimal "ensure mirror + one fetch" prelude, then extract script from the mirror: `git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"`.
2. `curl` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com.

The tricky thing: on the first post-merge run, the mirror contains the pre-merge tree — `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` doesn't exist in the pre-merge mirror either (until a fetch updates the mirror... wait, actually the mirror is a mirror of the GitHub repo. On the first post-merge run, if the mirror gets fetched/updated first, then `main:` in the mirror WOULD contain the script after fetch. But wait — the mirror could have fetched already? The mirror updates when CI runs. The first post-merge run happens because a push to main occurs; but does any job fetch the mirror before this one? Not necessarily.

Let me think carefully about the bootstrap options:

Option A: inline prelude — ensure mirror exists (clone if not), do one fetch, then extract `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` from the mirror's `main` branch and run it. On the first post-merge run, the inline fetch updates the mirror to post-merge main, so `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` exists. But if the fetch fails (network hiccup — exactly the incident scenario), the fallback would be... we can't fall back to recreate inline easily (that's the expensive path the script owns). Hmm, but the prelude is "cheap" per the reviewer. If the single inline fetch fails, we could fall back to extracting from whatever the mirror has (if the script exists in the mirror — it would from any run after this PR is merged... but on the first post-merge run the mirror might not have it). Actually wait — the mirror is persistent on the runner. After this PR merges and the first run does a fetch, the mirror has the script forever. But the FIRST post-merge run: the mirror's main may be at pre-merge commit. The inline prelude fetches; if fetch succeeds, mirror's main = post-merge, script exists. If fetch fails... we could then retry inline a few times, and if still failing, fall back to curl pinned to github.sha.

Option B: curl pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` — but wait, on PR runs `github.sha` is the PR's merge commit / head sha, which exists on GitHub (pushed), so raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/<sha>/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh works for PR runs too. On push-to-main events, github.sha is the pushed commit, which exists. So curl is simple and robust. But it requires network to raw.githubusercontent.com — the runners clearly have network (they clone from github.com). The concern in the incident was flaky network with retries needed. We can add retry to curl too.

Actually, the cleanest approach that reviewers suggested: keep an inline prelude in the workflow that ensures the mirror exists and does a single fetch, then extract the script from the mirror (`git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`), then run the extracted script which owns the resilient retry logic. But there's a subtlety: what if the mirror doesn't have the script on the very first post-merge run and fetch fails? Fallback to curl pinned to github.sha. Hmm, but that adds complexity.

Alternative robust approach used widely: `curl -fsSL --retry 5` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}`. Since the sha is pushed to GitHub, this works on both PR and post-merge runs. Simple, single mechanism. Add `--retry` with backoff for transient failures. This removes ALL workspace and mirror-state dependency.

But hold on — a concern with curl: the script being run would be from the PR head on PR runs (fine, it's being tested), and from the merged commit on post-merge runs (fine). The reviewer explicitly offered this option.

However, there's a security/review consideration: running a script fetched via curl pinned to the exact commit SHA is fine for this repo's own workflows.

Another option: extract from the mirror after an inline fetch prelude. The reviewer's first suggestion. Advantage: works offline-of-raw-content-domain; uses the mirror that the step itself maintains. Disadvantage: on the first post-merge run, if the inline fetch fails, there's no script to extract. But we could chain: try extract from mirror; if that fails, curl. Hmm.

Design: In each mirror step's run block:

```bash

MIRROR=...
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent

if [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
    echo "using scripts/update_git_mirror.sh from local mirror"

      "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" -o "$SCRIPT"
  fi
fi
bash "$SCRIPT" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

Wait — extracting from the mirror before fetching: the mirror may be stale (pre-merge) on first post-merge run, so `show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` fails → falls back to curl pinned to github.sha. On subsequent runs, mirror's main has the script (mirror gets updated by the script run itself — since it's a mirror, fetch origin updates refs/heads/main... actually a `--mirror` clone maps all refs; fetch origin updates main). So after the first successful run, the mirror path is used.

But hmm — actually should the step even fetch before extracting? The script itself does the fetch with retries. The extraction-from-mirror is a bootstrap optimization; curl fallback covers the cold case. That matches reviewer's suggestion #1 pattern (though they suggested fetching inline first — I think relying on the script's fetch is better: single owner of fetch logic).

Wait, one more consideration: what if `${{ github.sha }}` — in `pull_request` events it's the merge commit (refs/pull/N/merge), which is NOT pushed to the repo, so raw.githubusercontent.com/<sha> would 404! Hmm. Actually for `pull_request` events, github.sha is the test merge commit which exists only in the refs/pull namespace, not in the repo's branches. Does raw.githubusercontent.com resolve arbitrary reachable commits? No — raw.githubusercontent serves blobs by commit-ish that exists in the repo. refs/pull/... merge commits... Actually raw.githubusercontent.com does resolve any commit SHA that GitHub's backend knows for the repo, including PR merge commits? Let me think. raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/SHA/path uses the git data API backend; I believe it can serve any commit object reachable in the repository's object store, and PR refs are part of the repo. Actually, I recall that raw.githubusercontent can serve PR head SHAs (people use it for gists/branches). For PR merge commits (test merge), the object exists in the repo's odb (refs/pull/N/merge), so it should be resolvable. Hmm, but I'm not 100% sure raw content endpoint resolves non-branch/non-tag SHAs... Actually it does — raw.githubusercontent.com resolves full 40-char SHAs of any object in the repository database. Yes, this is commonly used (e.g., serving files at a specific commit SHA).

But do these workflows even run on pull_request? They're build workflows — check the triggers. build-macos.yml is likely workflow_dispatch / schedule (daily-publish). Let me check the `on:` triggers. If they're only push/schedule/dispatch, github.sha is always a real pushed commit. Let me check.

# ║    T6 a recreated mirror records the blob:none filter (gh-1477            ║

# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy

MODE="${1:-}"
SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ "$MODE" != "--legacy" ] && [ ! -f "$SCRIPT" ]; then

fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"

  if [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ]; then
    legacy_update_mirror "$@"
  else
    bash "$SCRIPT" "$@"
  fi
}

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {

  echo "$fail_clone" > "$dir/clone_left"

REAL_GIT="$REAL_GIT"
LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"
sub=""; skip=0

    -*) ;;
    *) sub="\$a"; break ;;

      echo "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected" >&2
      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2

make_fixture() {
  local d="$1"

export MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP=0

  local d="$WORK/t1"; mkdir -p "$d"; make_fixture "$d"

Key insight: both workflows are `workflow_dispatch` only. So `github.sha` is always the commit that was current on the branch when dispatched (for daily-publish dispatch, it's the main branch head at dispatch time — a real pushed commit, served by raw.githubusercontent.com). 

Now, plan of fixes:

**Fix 1 (BLOCKING threads 1+2): bootstrap the script without workspace dependency.**

Design for the YAML steps — shared pattern at all 3 call sites:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 rework review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
# self-hosted runners, so $GITHUB_WORKSPACE may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
# wiped) — never read scripts/ from the workspace here. Bootstrap the
# updater from the freshest available source: the commit-pinned raw URL
# (always resolvable — workflow_dispatch only), with the local mirror as a
# no-network fallback once it has the script; then its own retries own the
# resilience.
SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
if ! { curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" \
        -o "$SCRIPT" \
      || { git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null \
           && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; }; then
  echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (network down and mirror lacks the script)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
bash "$SCRIPT" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

Wait — ordering question: curl primary or mirror primary? I earlier reasoned curl-primary tests the PR's own version on dispatch of non-main refs and is deterministic. Since these workflows are dispatch-only, `github.sha` is the dispatched ref's head — resolvable on raw.githubusercontent.com. curl-primary it is, with mirror fallback (mirror works even if raw CDN is blocked).

Hmm, but one concern: `curl --retry-all-errors` requires curl 7.71+. macOS runners with homebrew curl — likely fine; but system curl on older macOS? Sequoia ships curl 8.x? Actually macOS's /usr/bin/curl is 8.x on recent macOS, but older runners could have 7.64. `--retry-all-errors` was added in curl 7.71.0 (June 2020). macOS 12+ ships curl 7.77+. Safe enough. But to be extra safe I could drop `--retry-all-errors` and use just `--retry 5`. With `-f` and `--retry`, HTTP 5xx and transient errors retry; connection failures retry too. `--retry-all-errors` also retries 4xx which we don't want anyway (404 = bad pin, retrying won't help). Actually with --retry (without --retry-all-errors), curl retries on transient errors: timeouts, FTP errors, HTTP 408/429/5xx, connection refused/reset... A DNS failure isn't retried without --retry-all-errors. I'll keep `--retry-all-errors` for DNS-type transients — curl 7.71+ is a reasonable floor for these macOS runners (gh runners use recent macOS images).

Also use `${RUNNER_TEMP}` — guaranteed on Actions runners.

```

Alternative: reviewer option 1 (fetch inline first, then extract from mirror). I considered it; curl-primary + mirror-fallback covers all cases with one code path. Good.

AGENTS.md
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one

t8() {

  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1
  local before
  before=$(mirror_head "$d/mirror.git")
  make_shim "$d/shim" 99 99   # every fetch AND every clone fails
  use_shim "$d/shim"
  local out rc

        update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" 2>&1); rc=$?

  update_mirror "file://$d/remote.git" "$d/mirror.git" >/dev/null 2>&1

  extracted="$d/extracted.sh"
  git --git-dir="$d/mirror.git" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh \

  rc=$?

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

### Thread 1 — `.github/workflows/build-macos.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

```bash

git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

or pull the script pinned to the run's commit:

```bash

### Thread 3 — `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):
💡 **SUGGESTION: recreate into a temp dir and swap on success — a failed recreate currently destroys the last good mirror**

`recreate_mirror` does `rm -rf "$mirror"` before every clone attempt, so if all `MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS` fail (e.g. the fetch retries were exhausted by a short remote outage and the recreate then hits a mid-transfer drop — the gh-1644 incident shape), the script exits leaving **no mirror at all**, not even the stale-but-valid one it deleted. The checkout step could still have succeeded against the old mirror (`git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 <url>` pulls the tip from origin anyway).

Cloning into a sibling and swapping on success keeps a known-good mirror across a failed recreate:

```bash
local tmp="$mirror.recreate"
rm -rf "$tmp"
if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then

  mv "$tmp" "$mirror"

Not blocking — with blobless clones the recreate window is minutes, and the partial-dir cleanup contract (T5) is preserved either way.

# pr-1665: gh-1644 [daily-publish] cli leg failed

## Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

blocks.text:
Now I understand the fix required. The blocking issue: mirror update steps run before any checkout, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` depends on workspace content. The reviewer suggested two bootstrap options:

1. Inline minimal "ensure mirror + one fetch" prelude, then extract script from the mirror: `git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"`.
2. `curl` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com.

The tricky thing: on the first post-merge run, the mirror contains the pre-merge tree — `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` doesn't exist in the pre-merge mirror either (until a fetch updates the mirror... wait, actually the mirror is a mirror of the GitHub repo. On the first post-merge run, if the mirror gets fetched/updated first, then `main:` in the mirror WOULD contain the script after fetch. But wait — the mirror could have fetched already? The mirror updates when CI runs. The first post-merge run happens because a push to main occurs; but does any job fetch the mirror before this one? Not necessarily.

Let me think carefully about the bootstrap options:

Option A: inline prelude — ensure mirror exists (clone if not), do one fetch, then extract `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` from the mirror's `main` branch and run it. On the first post-merge run, the inline fetch updates the mirror to post-merge main, so `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` exists. But if the fetch fails (network hiccup — exactly the incident scenario), the fallback would be... we can't fall back to recreate inline easily (that's the expensive path the script owns). Hmm, but the prelude is "cheap" per the reviewer. If the single inline fetch fails, we could fall back to extracting from whatever the mirror has (if the script exists in the mirror — it would from any run after this PR is merged... but on the first post-merge run the mirror might not have it). Actually wait — the mirror is persistent on the runner. After this PR merges and the first run does a fetch, the mirror has the script forever. But the FIRST post-merge run: the mirror's main may be at pre-merge commit. The inline prelude fetches; if fetch succeeds, mirror's main = post-merge, script exists. If fetch fails... we could then retry inline a few times, and if still failing, fall back to curl pinned to github.sha.

Option B: curl pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` — but wait, on PR runs `github.sha` is the PR's merge commit / head sha, which exists on GitHub (pushed), so raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/<sha>/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh works for PR runs too. On push-to-main events, github.sha is the pushed commit, which exists. So curl is simple and robust. But it requires network to raw.githubusercontent.com — the runners clearly have network (they clone from github.com). The concern in the incident was flaky network with retries needed. We can add retry to curl too.

Actually, the cleanest approach that reviewers suggested: keep an inline prelude in the workflow that ensures the mirror exists and does a single fetch, then extract the script from the mirror (`git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`), then run the extracted script which owns the resilient retry logic. But there's a subtlety: what if the mirror doesn't have the script on the very first post-merge run and fetch fails? Fallback to curl pinned to github.sha. Hmm, but that adds complexity.

Alternative robust approach used widely: `curl -fsSL --retry 5` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}`. Since the sha is pushed to GitHub, this works on both PR and post-merge runs. Simple, single mechanism. Add `--retry` with backoff for transient failures. This removes ALL workspace and mirror-state dependency.

But hold on — a concern with curl: the script being run would be from the PR head on PR runs (fine, it's being tested), and from the merged commit on post-merge runs (fine). The reviewer explicitly offered this option.

However, there's a security/review consideration: running a script fetched via curl pinned to the exact commit SHA is fine for this repo's own workflows.

Another option: extract from the mirror after an inline fetch prelude. The reviewer's first suggestion. Advantage: works offline-of-raw-content-domain; uses the mirror that the step itself maintains. Disadvantage: on the first post-merge run, if the inline fetch fails, there's no script to extract. But we could chain: try extract from mirror; if that fails, curl. Hmm.

Let me pick one coherent design and apply it uniformly to all 3 call sites:

Design: In each mirror step's run block:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
MIRROR=...
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
# self-hosted runners, so the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
# wiped) — never read scripts/ from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE here. Bootstrap the
# updater from the freshly-synced mirror, falling back to the commit-pinned
# raw URL; then the script's own retries own the resilience.
SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
    echo "using scripts/update_git_mirror.sh from local mirror"
  else
    curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \

On subsequent runs, mirror's main has the script (mirror gets updated by the script run itself — since it's a mirror, fetch origin updates refs/heads/main... actually a `--mirror` clone maps all refs; fetch origin updates main). So after the first successful run, the mirror path is used.

But hmm — actually should the step even fetch before extracting? The script itself does the fetch with retries. The extraction-from-mirror is a bootstrap optimization; curl fallback covers the cold case. That matches reviewer's suggestion #1 pattern (though they suggested fetching inline first — I think relying on the script's fetch is better: single owner of fetch logic).

Wait, one more consideration: what if `${{ github.sha }}` — in `pull_request` events it's the merge commit (refs/pull/N/merge), which is NOT pushed to the repo, so raw.githubusercontent.com/<sha> would 404! Hmm. Actually for `pull_request` events, github.sha is the test merge commit which exists only in the refs/pull namespace, not in the repo's branches. Does raw.githubusercontent.com resolve arbitrary reachable commits? No — raw.githubusercontent serves blobs by commit-ish that exists in the repo. refs/pull/... merge commits... Actually raw.githubusercontent.com does resolve any commit SHA that GitHub's backend knows for the repo, including PR merge commits? Let me think. raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/SHA/path uses the git data API backend; I believe it can serve any commit object reachable in the repository's object store, and PR refs are part of the repo. Actually, I recall that raw.githubusercontent can serve PR head SHAs (people use it for gists/branches). For PR merge commits (test merge), the object exists in the repo's odb (refs/pull/N/merge), so it should be resolvable. Hmm, but I'm not 100% sure raw content endpoint resolves non-branch/non-tag SHAs... Actually it does — raw.githubusercontent.com resolves full 40-char SHAs of any object in the repository database. Yes, this is commonly used (e.g., serving files at a specific commit SHA).

# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy

SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"

fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {

LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"

    -*) ;;

      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2

Key insight: both workflows are `workflow_dispatch` only. So `github.sha` is always the commit that was current on the branch when dispatched (for daily-publish dispatch, it's the main branch head at dispatch time — a real pushed commit, served by raw.githubusercontent.com). 

Now, plan of fixes:

**Fix 1 (BLOCKING threads 1+2): bootstrap the script without workspace dependency.**

Design for the YAML steps — shared pattern at all 3 call sites:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 rework review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
# self-hosted runners, so $GITHUB_WORKSPACE may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
# wiped) — never read scripts/ from the workspace here. Bootstrap the
# updater from the freshest available source: the commit-pinned raw URL
# (always resolvable — workflow_dispatch only), with the local mirror as a
# no-network fallback once it has the script; then its own retries own the
# resilience.
SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
if ! { curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" \
        -o "$SCRIPT" \
      || { git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null \
           && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; }; then
  echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (network down and mirror lacks the script)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
bash "$SCRIPT" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

Wait — ordering question: curl primary or mirror primary? I earlier reasoned curl-primary tests the PR's own version on dispatch of non-main refs and is deterministic. Since these workflows are dispatch-only, `github.sha` is the dispatched ref's head — resolvable on raw.githubusercontent.com. curl-primary it is, with mirror fallback (mirror works even if raw CDN is blocked).

Hmm, but one concern: `curl --retry-all-errors` requires curl 7.71+. macOS runners with homebrew curl — likely fine; but system curl on older macOS? Sequoia ships curl 8.x? Actually macOS's /usr/bin/curl is 8.x on recent macOS, but older runners could have 7.64. `--retry-all-errors` was added in curl 7.71.0 (June 2020). macOS 12+ ships curl 7.77+. Safe enough. But to be extra safe I could drop `--retry-all-errors` and use just `--retry 5`. With `-f` and `--retry`, HTTP 5xx and transient errors retry; connection failures retry too. `--retry-all-errors` also retries 4xx which we don't want anyway (404 = bad pin, retrying won't help). Actually with --retry (without --retry-all-errors), curl retries on transient errors: timeouts, FTP errors, HTTP 408/429/5xx, connection refused/reset... A DNS failure isn't retried without --retry-all-errors. I'll keep `--retry-all-errors` for DNS-type transients — curl 7.71+ is a reasonable floor for these macOS runners (gh runners use recent macOS images).

Also use `${RUNNER_TEMP}` — guaranteed on Actions runners.

One more subtlety: `set -euo pipefail` + `if ! { ...; }` — the `curl ... || { ...; }` inside braces; if curl fails and mirror extraction succeeds, fine. fi

```

# AGENTS.md

## Project layout

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
}

- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T10:27:39Z

## PR Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-17):
🚨 **BLOCKING: `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` runs before any checkout — on the first post-merge run the script does not exist in the workspace**

This step is the **first step** of the `build-macos` job (and the same pattern at `build-mobile.yml:625` `build-ios` and `build-mobile.yml:1059` `submit-ios`): no `actions/checkout` precedes it, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` resolves relative to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. On these **persistent self-hosted runners** the workspace is not cleaned between runs — the proof is the very next step (`Checkout repository from local mirrors`), which does `rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" && mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"` because a previous clone is sitting there.

So on the **first run after this PR merges**, `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` contains the previous run's clone — a **pre-merge tree without `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`**. The step fails with `bash: scripts/update_git_mirror.sh: No such file or directory` (exit 127) before the resilience logic ever runs. All four affected legs (build-macos arm64/x86_64, build-ios, submit-ios) go red once, and gh-1644 — which auto-closes only when the leg goes green — stays open. The old inline logic had no workspace dependency; the fix introduces one.

(If the runner were instead configured to wipe the workspace, the step fails the same way — only a post-merge workspace makes this line work.)

Suggested fix — bootstrap the script without depending on the checked-out tree, e.g. after a minimal inline "ensure mirror exists + one fetch" prelude (cheap; the script's retries still own the resilience):

bash "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

```bash

# pr-1665: gh-1644 [daily-publish] cli leg failed

## Description

Closes #1644
## Root Cause

Two independent failures in the daily-publish `cli` leg (run 38855793382):

- **Size budget gate**: `browser_ext/dart` path-depends on the root package, so `sw/agent.js` grows with root-`lib/` features; ~18 commits since the 10-14 floor reseed pushed it to +5.3% vs the +5.0% budget (local rebuild reproduced 1887086 bytes byte-identically). Legitimate growth — the gate's reseed escape hatch applies.
- **`Update local git mirrors` (both macOS archs)**: single-shot fetch with swallowed stderr, then a full `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died on a transient network drop (`error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected`, exit 128) — no retry, no partial-dir cleanup. Same pattern in `build-mobile.yml` (build-ios + submit-ios).

## Fix

- `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` (new): fetch retries with visible stderr + stall abort; recreation via blobless `git clone --mirror --filter=blob:none` (gh-1477 precedent — minutes, not ~1 h; `--reference --depth=1` checkouts pull tip blobs from origin) with retries and partial-dir cleanup; `::error::` + nonzero exit on exhaustion. All 3 mirror steps in `build-macos.yml`/`build-mobile.yml` now call it.
- `scripts/size_budget/fa-extension.tsv`: reseeded from a real `--with-app` artifact at HEAD (agent.js 1791532→1887086, main.dart.js +4.6%, +2 inappwebview rows, −removed skills assets, TOTAL→73347265).

## Test Coverage

- `scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh` (new): 7 scenarios (fixture remotes + fault-injecting `git` shim) — fetch retry recovers with NO recreate, persistent failure exits nonzero after exactly N attempts, poisoned dirs recover, `blob:none` recorded; `--legacy` mode replays the incident against the verbatim pre-fix logic → dies exit 128 (repro confirmed). 7/7 + 4/4 PASS incl. fresh-cwd/clean-env parity; live github.com clone+fetch cycle verified.
- Size gate: pre-fix `check` failed with the exact CI signature; post-reseed exit 0; `size_manifest.py selftest` PASS; YAML parse + `bash -n` on all touched `run:` blocks.

## Notes

- No Dart code changed; existing runner mirrors stay full — only recreations become blobless. Next bundle breach is a routine conscious reseed (gh-1570 precedent).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)…

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# update_git_mirror.sh — resilient local git-mirror update (gh-1644).
#
# Replaces the single-shot inline logic in build-macos.yml / build-mobile.yml
# ("Update local git mirror(s)" steps). The old logic fetched ONCE with
# stderr swallowed (`2>/dev/null`), and on any failure fell through to a
# FULL `git clone --mirror` whose ~1 h transfer died mid-flight on the
# self-hosted runner's flaky link (run 38855793382:
# "error: 2931 bytes of body are still expected", exit 128) — no retry,
# and a killed clone left a partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Contract (asserted by scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh):
#   - fetch retries MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS times (default 3) with
#     MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP seconds (default 10) between attempts, stderr
#     visible — the first-failure cause is no longer swallowed;
#   - each attempt aborts on a stalled connection (<1 KB/s for 60 s) so a
#     wedged transfer engages the bounded retries instead of holding the
#     step for an hour;
#   - persistent fetch failure → recreate. The partial dir is removed
#     before EVERY attempt (a killed clone leaves a non-repo dir that
#     would fail the next attempt with "already exists"), and the
#     recreation is a BLOBLESS mirror (`--filter=blob:none` — the gh-1477
#     precedent in this repo): commits/trees only, ~90% less transfer,
#     shrinking the recreate window from ~1 h to minutes. The dependent
#     checkouts use `git clone --reference <mirror> --depth=1` and pull
#     tip blobs from origin, so they never need historical blobs from the
#     mirror. An EXISTING full mirror is untouched — fetches stay cheap;
#     only recreations become blobless;
#   - recreation retries MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS times (default 3);
#   - every failure path exits nonzero with a ::error annotation and
#     leaves NO partial mirror dir behind.
#
# Usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>
# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh URL MIRROR
set -euo pipefail

url="${1:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"
mirror="${2:?usage: update_git_mirror.sh <url> <mirror-path>}"

fetch_attempts="${MIRROR_FETCH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
clone_attempts="${MIRROR_CLONE_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
retry_sleep="${MIRROR_RETRY_SLEEP:-10}"

# Stall guard for http(s) remotes (no-op for file/local remotes): an
# attempt moving <1 KB/s for 60 s is dead — retry instead of hanging.
# The run-38855793382 death was a 62-minute transfer ending in
# "2931 bytes of body are still expected".
STALL_GUARD=(-c http.lowSpeedLimit=1000 -c http.lowSpeedTime=60)

is_repo() { git -C "$1" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; }

recreate_mirror() {
  local attempt
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$mirror"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$mirror"; then
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$mirror"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s)" >&2
  return 1
}

if [ -d "$mirror" ] && is_repo "$mirror"; then
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= fetch_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "fetch attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts}: $mirror"
    if git -C "$mirror" "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" fetch origin; then
      echo "mirror updated: $mirror"
      exit 0
    fi
    echo "git fetch failed (attempt ${attempt}/${fetch_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$fetch_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  echo "git fetch failed after ${fetch_attempts} attempt(s) — recreating the mirror" >&2
fi

recreate_mirror

blocks.text:
Now I understand the fix required. The blocking issue: mirror update steps run before any checkout, so `bash scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` depends on workspace content. The reviewer suggested two bootstrap options:

1. Inline minimal "ensure mirror + one fetch" prelude, then extract script from the mirror: `git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"`.
2. `curl` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` from raw.githubusercontent.com.

The tricky thing: on the first post-merge run, the mirror contains the pre-merge tree — `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` doesn't exist in the pre-merge mirror either (until a fetch updates the mirror... wait, actually the mirror is a mirror of the GitHub repo. On the first post-merge run, if the mirror gets fetched/updated first, then `main:` in the mirror WOULD contain the script after fetch. But wait — the mirror could have fetched already? The mirror updates when CI runs. The first post-merge run happens because a push to main occurs; but does any job fetch the mirror before this one? Not necessarily.

Let me think carefully about the bootstrap options:

Option A: inline prelude — ensure mirror exists (clone if not), do one fetch, then extract `scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` from the mirror's `main` branch and run it. On the first post-merge run, the inline fetch updates the mirror to post-merge main, so `main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh` exists. But if the fetch fails (network hiccup — exactly the incident scenario), the fallback would be... we can't fall back to recreate inline easily (that's the expensive path the script owns). Hmm, but the prelude is "cheap" per the reviewer. If the single inline fetch fails, we could fall back to extracting from whatever the mirror has (if the script exists in the mirror — it would from any run after this PR is merged... but on the first post-merge run the mirror might not have it). Actually wait — the mirror is persistent on the runner. After this PR merges and the first run does a fetch, the mirror has the script forever. But the FIRST post-merge run: the mirror's main may be at pre-merge commit. The inline prelude fetches; if fetch succeeds, mirror's main = post-merge, script exists. If fetch fails... we could then retry inline a few times, and if still failing, fall back to curl pinned to github.sha.

Option B: curl pinned to `${{ github.sha }}` — but wait, on PR runs `github.sha` is the PR's merge commit / head sha, which exists on GitHub (pushed), so raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/<sha>/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh works for PR runs too. On push-to-main events, github.sha is the pushed commit, which exists. So curl is simple and robust. But it requires network to raw.githubusercontent.com — the runners clearly have network (they clone from github.com). The concern in the incident was flaky network with retries needed. We can add retry to curl too.

Actually, the cleanest approach that reviewers suggested: keep an inline prelude in the workflow that ensures the mirror exists and does a single fetch, then extract the script from the mirror (`git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh`), then run the extracted script which owns the resilient retry logic. But there's a subtlety: what if the mirror doesn't have the script on the very first post-merge run and fetch fails? Fallback to curl pinned to github.sha. Hmm, but that adds complexity.

Alternative robust approach used widely: `curl -fsSL --retry 5` the script pinned to `${{ github.sha }}`. Since the sha is pushed to GitHub, this works on both PR and post-merge runs. Simple, single mechanism. Add `--retry` with backoff for transient failures. This removes ALL workspace and mirror-state dependency.

But hold on — a concern with curl: the script being run would be from the PR head on PR runs (fine, it's being tested), and from the merged commit on post-merge runs (fine). The reviewer explicitly offered this option.

However, there's a security/review consideration: running a script fetched via curl pinned to the exact commit SHA is fine for this repo's own workflows.

Another option: extract from the mirror after an inline fetch prelude. The reviewer's first suggestion. Advantage: works offline-of-raw-content-domain; uses the mirror that the step itself maintains. Disadvantage: on the first post-merge run, if the inline fetch fails, there's no script to extract. But we could chain: try extract from mirror; if that fails, curl. Hmm.

Let me pick one coherent design and apply it uniformly to all 3 call sites:

Design: In each mirror step's run block:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
MIRROR=...
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
# self-hosted runners, so the workspace may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
# wiped) — never read scripts/ from $GITHUB_WORKSPACE here. Bootstrap the
# updater from the freshly-synced mirror, falling back to the commit-pinned
# raw URL; then the script's own retries own the resilience.
SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
if [ ! -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
  if [ -d "$MIRROR" ] && git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; then
    echo "using scripts/update_git_mirror.sh from local mirror"
  else
    curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \

On subsequent runs, mirror's main has the script (mirror gets updated by the script run itself — since it's a mirror, fetch origin updates refs/heads/main... actually a `--mirror` clone maps all refs; fetch origin updates main). So after the first successful run, the mirror path is used.

But hmm — actually should the step even fetch before extracting? The script itself does the fetch with retries. The extraction-from-mirror is a bootstrap optimization; curl fallback covers the cold case. That matches reviewer's suggestion #1 pattern (though they suggested fetching inline first — I think relying on the script's fetch is better: single owner of fetch logic).

Wait, one more consideration: what if `${{ github.sha }}` — in `pull_request` events it's the merge commit (refs/pull/N/merge), which is NOT pushed to the repo, so raw.githubusercontent.com/<sha> would 404! Hmm. Actually for `pull_request` events, github.sha is the test merge commit which exists only in the refs/pull namespace, not in the repo's branches. Does raw.githubusercontent.com resolve arbitrary reachable commits? No — raw.githubusercontent serves blobs by commit-ish that exists in the repo. refs/pull/... merge commits... Actually raw.githubusercontent.com does resolve any commit SHA that GitHub's backend knows for the repo, including PR merge commits? Let me think. raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/repo/SHA/path uses the git data API backend; I believe it can serve any commit object reachable in the repository's object store, and PR refs are part of the repo. Actually, I recall that raw.githubusercontent can serve PR head SHAs (people use it for gists/branches). For PR merge commits (test merge), the object exists in the repo's odb (refs/pull/N/merge), so it should be resolvable. Hmm, but I'm not 100% sure raw content endpoint resolves non-branch/non-tag SHAs... Actually it does — raw.githubusercontent.com resolves full 40-char SHAs of any object in the repository database. Yes, this is commonly used (e.g., serving files at a specific commit SHA).

# Run from anywhere:  bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh
# Legacy replay:      bash scripts/update_git_mirror_selftest.sh --legacy

SCRIPT="scripts/update_git_mirror.sh"

fail=0
ok()   { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "✅ $1"; }
bad()  { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "❌ $1" >&2; }
label_legacy() { [ "$MODE" = "--legacy" ] && echo "legacy" || echo "script"; }

# ── pre-fix inline logic (the bug), verbatim from the old workflow step ────
legacy_update_mirror() {
  local url="$1" mirror="$2"

# ── fault-injecting git shim: fails the first N fetch/clone calls with ─────
# ── the incident's error signature, then delegates to the real git ─────────
make_shim() {

LEFT="$(cd "$dir" && pwd)"

    -*) ;;

      echo "fatal: early EOF" >&2

Key insight: both workflows are `workflow_dispatch` only. So `github.sha` is always the commit that was current on the branch when dispatched (for daily-publish dispatch, it's the main branch head at dispatch time — a real pushed commit, served by raw.githubusercontent.com). 

Now, plan of fixes:

**Fix 1 (BLOCKING threads 1+2): bootstrap the script without workspace dependency.**

Design for the YAML steps — shared pattern at all 3 call sites:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$MIRROR")"
# gh-1644 rework review: this step runs BEFORE any checkout on persistent
# self-hosted runners, so $GITHUB_WORKSPACE may hold a pre-merge tree (or be
# wiped) — never read scripts/ from the workspace here. Bootstrap the
# updater from the freshest available source: the commit-pinned raw URL
# (always resolvable — workflow_dispatch only), with the local mirror as a
# no-network fallback once it has the script; then its own retries own the
# resilience.
SCRIPT="$RUNNER_TEMP/update_git_mirror.sh"
if ! { curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/${{ github.sha }}/scripts/update_git_mirror.sh" \
        -o "$SCRIPT" \
      || { git --git-dir="$MIRROR" show main:scripts/update_git_mirror.sh > "$SCRIPT" 2>/dev/null \
           && [ -s "$SCRIPT" ]; }; then
  echo "::error::could not bootstrap update_git_mirror.sh (network down and mirror lacks the script)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
bash "$SCRIPT" https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$MIRROR"
```

Wait — ordering question: curl primary or mirror primary? I earlier reasoned curl-primary tests the PR's own version on dispatch of non-main refs and is deterministic. Since these workflows are dispatch-only, `github.sha` is the dispatched ref's head — resolvable on raw.githubusercontent.com. curl-primary it is, with mirror fallback (mirror works even if raw CDN is blocked).

Hmm, but one concern: `curl --retry-all-errors` requires curl 7.71+. macOS runners with homebrew curl — likely fine; but system curl on older macOS? Sequoia ships curl 8.x? Actually macOS's /usr/bin/curl is 8.x on recent macOS, but older runners could have 7.64. `--retry-all-errors` was added in curl 7.71.0 (June 2020). macOS 12+ ships curl 7.77+. Safe enough. But to be extra safe I could drop `--retry-all-errors` and use just `--retry 5`. With `-f` and `--retry`, HTTP 5xx and transient errors retry; connection failures retry too. `--retry-all-errors` also retries 4xx which we don't want anyway (404 = bad pin, retrying won't help). Actually with --retry (without --retry-all-errors), curl retries on transient errors: timeouts, FTP errors, HTTP 408/429/5xx, connection refused/reset... A DNS failure isn't retried without --retry-all-errors. I'll keep `--retry-all-errors` for DNS-type transients — curl 7.71+ is a reasonable floor for these macOS runners (gh runners use recent macOS images).

Also use `${RUNNER_TEMP}` — guaranteed on Actions runners.

One more subtlety: `set -euo pipefail` + `if ! { ...; }` — the `curl ... || { ...; }` inside braces; if curl fails and mirror extraction succeeds, fine. fi

```

# AGENTS.md

## Project layout

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

{"newText":"recreate_mirror() {
  # Clone into a sibling and swap on success: a failed recreate must not
  # destroy the last good mirror (gh-1665 review thread 3).
  local attempt tmp="$mirror.recreate"
  for ((attempt = 1; attempt <= clone_attempts; attempt++)); do
    echo "recreate attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts}: $mirror"
    rm -rf "$tmp"
    if git "${STALL_GUARD[@]}" clone --mirror --filter=blob:none "$url" "$tmp"; then
      rm -rf "$mirror"
      mv "$tmp" "$mirror"
      echo "mirror recreated: $mirror (blobless)"
      return 0
    fi
    echo "git clone --mirror failed (attempt ${attempt}/${clone_attempts})" >&2
    if [ "$attempt" -lt "$clone_attempts" ]; then
      sleep "$retry_sleep"
    fi
  done
  rm -rf "$tmp"   # never leave a partial clone behind
  echo "::error::update_git_mirror: recreating $mirror from $url failed after ${clone_attempts} attempt(s) — last good mirror preserved" >&2
  return 1
